Personally, I believe this cycle will be much longer than the previous ones, but the final drawdown will end up being relatively similar.

Hope you understand

quote.text:
Bitcoin is 410 days past its all-time high, and it is down 50%.

At the same point in previous cycles:

2013 cycle: -80%
2017 cycle: -82%
2021 cycle: -75%

Peak-to-trough declines in those cycles: -85%, -83% and -77%. Each bottom came 12 to 14 months after the peak.

So far, this cycle's low is -53%, set on June 30, 2026.

This drawdown is shallower than any previous one.

Whether that reflects a more mature market or a cycle that is not finished yet is the open question. $BTC

tweets.text:
I know this sounds strange, but I'm hoping the stock market will dump further (and yes I own a lot of stocks so I also feel this pain).

Not a crash, just enough pressure.

Right now the market is almost certain the Fed hikes again in December.

The only thing that really changes their mind is when markets start breaking:

Stocks down
Bonds up
Yields falling

That tells the Fed they're tightening too much.

It happened in 2018, and 2019 became a great year for BTC.

Painful first, bullish after.

Are we about to see the same playbook?
